Brake System Specification

System Overview

The Emergency Braking System shall provide safe and predictable deceleration under all supported operating conditions.

The system continuously evaluates vehicle speed, requested brake pressure and actual brake pressure to determine the required braking mode.

Warning

In operating modes where vehicle.speed > 5 km/h, emergency braking has highest priority and shall override NORMAL_BRAKE_REQUEST.

Important Information

Note

Changes to BRK-001 or BRK-002 require an independent safety review before approval.

Braking Behaviour

The controller shall evaluate the following conditions during every 10 ms control cycle:

IF brake_request == ACTIVE
   AND vehicle_speed > 5
   AND pressure_actual < pressure_target
THEN
   braking_mode := EMERGENCY_BRAKING
   diagnostic_state := PRESSURE_FAULT

When EMERGENCY_BRAKING is activated, the controller shall transition the braking system into SAFE_STATE if the requested pressure cannot be achieved within 500 ms.

Caution

Changing FAULT_DEBOUNCE_COUNT from 3 to 5 increases the maximum fault detection time from 30 ms to 50 ms.

This change affects the safety assumptions of BRK-001 and therefore requires a new safety review.

System States

The braking system can operate in the following states:

  1. NORMAL_OPERATION

  2. BRAKE_REQUESTED

  3. PRESSURE_BUILDUP

  4. BRAKING_ACTIVE

  5. EMERGENCY_BRAKING

  6. SAFE_STATE

A transition from BRAKING_ACTIVE to EMERGENCY_BRAKING shall occur when:

pressure_actual < (pressure_target * 0.85)

and:

vehicle_speed > 5

Recovery Conditions

Recovery from SAFE_STATE is permitted only when all of the following conditions are satisfied:

  1. vehicle_speed == 0

  2. brake_request == RELEASED

  3. pressure_actual >= MIN_SAFE_PRESSURE

  4. diagnostic_state != PRESSURE_FAULT

Important

If any of the recovery conditions evaluate to FALSE, the system shall remain in SAFE_STATE.

Review Impact

Attention

A modification to MAX_PRESSURE_DEVIATION, FAULT_DEBOUNCE_COUNT or MIN_SAFE_PRESSURE may indirectly change the behaviour of multiple requirements.

The reviewer shall therefore verify the rendered specification and not only the individual source-line changes.
